Definition: a form of G1507; to coil or wrap:--fold up.
BiblicalUsage: Helisso means to coil up, to fold like a garment, and it appears twice, both times for the heavens themselves. In Hebrews 1:12 the Lord will fold the heavens up as a vesture and they shall be changed, and in Revelation 6:14 the heaven departs as a scroll when it is rolled together.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the picture is meant to steady me: the heavens are not eternal, they are a garment God can fold, and the one who folds them is the same yesterday, today and for ever.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
